title: Renewal Readiness Sprint Kit: QBR Decks + Tracker
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact sprint kit to produce two QBR deck templates (Standard / Enterprise), a renewal conversation playbook, and an operational renewal-readiness tracker. Goal: create reproducible, play-tested assets that CSMs can use for high-velocity renewals (SMB/scale) and longer-cycle enterprise accounts. This doc is a working draft — use as the single source for the 2-week design + pilot sprint.

Intended audience:
- CSMs preparing QBRs
- CS leadership reviewing renewal approach
- Solutions/SEs who support enterprise conversations
- Customer Success Operations (for tracker implementation)

When to use:
- Standard template: accounts with < $50k ARR or 6–12 month renew cadence. Lightweight, outcome-focused, 8–12 slides.
- Enterprise template: strategic accounts with > $250k ARR or multi-product contracts. Deep-dive, 12–18 slides, includes risk & exec ask framing.

Sprint overview (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): collect 6 recent QBRs, top renewal objections list, and 3 exemplar enterprise decks. Assign pilot accounts.
- Week 1: produce first-pass Standard + Enterprise decks, build tracker schema, draft playbook. Internal review mid-week.
- Week 2: pilot with 2 CSMs, iterate on slide content and playbook phrasing, finalize tracker column keys and filters.
Owners: Priya (CS Ops PM), Daniel (CS Lead), Marisol (Content + Playbook), Evan (data & tracker).

Standard deck skeleton (8–12 slides) — concise flow with speaker notes:
1) Title + Outcome Statement (1 slide)
   - Headline: "QBR: [Customer] — 90-day outcomes & renewal ask"
   - Speaker note: one-sentence purpose + specific renewal checkpoint (e.g., renewal month)
2) Executive summary / Health snapshot (1)
   - NPS/usage trend/ARR-impact / top 3 accomplishments
   - Note: keep to 3 bullets, tie each to business value
3) Product adoption highlights (2)
   - Key workflows adopted, adoption curve charts (DAU/MAU or seats), top users
   - Call out any lift from Redwood features (e.g., dedicated routing)
4) Outcomes & business impact (2)
   - Quantified outcomes tied to KPIs (time saved, cost avoided, revenue influenced)
5) Risks & mitigation (1)
   - Current issues, severity, owner, ETA for fix
6) Renewal health & timeline (1)
   - Renewal month, likely outcome (green/amber/red), asks from customer
7) Suggested renewal proposal (1)
   - Three options (base, recommended, expansion) with bullets on value tradeoffs
8) Next steps & commitments (1)
   - Clear owner and dates; request for decision/steering committee if needed

Enterprise deck skeleton (12–18 slides) — deeper, relationship-focused:
1) Cover + tailored outcome statement (customized for the Exec audience)
2) Strategic context: customer goals & market pressures (1)
3) Executive summary + recommended renewal posture (1)
4) Platform ROI / value realization (2)
   - Multi-quarter view, integration uplift, cost-per-inference metrics where available
5) Adoption & stakeholder map (2)
   - Functional owners, exec sponsors, blockers per persona
6) Product deep dive (2)
   - Model variants used, latency/cost tradeoff choices, observability highlights
7) Risk register & remediation plan (2)
   - Severity, impact to business outcomes, mitigation timeline
8) Contract options & pricing motion (2)
   - Renewal scenarios: renew-as-is, reserved capacity, private deployment pilot
9) Ask matrix & decision calendar (1)
   - Who signs, procurement timeline, legal approvals needed
10) Case studies / expansion use-cases (1)
11) Appendix: technical clarifications, SSO/KMS status, audit logs (variable)

Speaker tips (enterprise): Always open with the customer’s top business objective. For execs, lead with impact metrics and procurement asks, not feature lists.

Renewal conversation playbook (script highlights):
- Opening: "Quick check — since our last QBR we've seen X outcome. Before we jump into detail, are there any strategic changes on your side that should change how we approach the renewal?"
- Value reinforcement: walk through 3 concrete wins, attach numbers where possible.
- Objection handling (pricing): "I hear budget pressure. Two pathways we recommend: (1) lock current price now with a phased expansion to defer spend, or (2) shift to a Reserved capacity model to lower per-token economics. Which would be easier for your finance team?"
- Escalation trigger: if procurement requests > 30 days, flag as "Negotiation" risk and pull in Solutions/Account Executive.

Renewal readiness tracker schema (column definitions):
- Account (string)
- ARR band (string)
- Renewal date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Owner (CSM)
- Health score (0-100)
- Risk level (Green|Amber|Red)
- Primary blocker (string)
- Exec sponsor (name & email)
- Procurement stage (Not started|In review|Signed)
- Suggested motion (Standard|Reserved|Private)
- Last QBR date
- Next meeting scheduled (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Ask value (USD)
- Notes (free text)
- Linked assets (Slides/Confluence/JIRA ids)

Risk scoring quick rubric (example):
- Health score < 60 => Amber/Red depending on trend
- Procurement stage not started and Renewal date < 45 days => +30 risk points
- Open severity-two or higher incident within 90 days => +20 risk points
- No Exec sponsor confirmed => +15 risk points
Scoring thresholds: 0-29 low, 30-59 medium, 60+ high risk. (We should finalize weights in CS Ops spreadsheet).

Operational notes for CS Ops (implementation hints):
- Tracker should be a single-source-of-truth Google Sheet connected to Looker/BigQuery for dashboards. Automate health score refresh from telemetry (DAU, errors, latency).
- Add filters: renewal quarter, owner, risk level, product line.
- Create Slack alert: when Risk level flips to Red, post to #cs-renewals with account + owner.

Pilot plan & success metrics:
- Pilot with 6 accounts across two segments (3 standard, 3 enterprise).
- Success metrics: reduction in approval time (procurement), % renewals closed at or above baseline price, CSM reported confidence score > 4/5.

Appendix: sample slide headlines and one-liners (copy-paste friendly):
- "Customer X: 3 outcomes in 90 days — Efficiency, Accuracy, Scale"
- "Platform ROI: 18% reduction in inference cost vs. last quarter"
- "Adoption: 42% seat growth in Product Intelligence team"
- "Risk: Integration latency spike — mitigation shipped 2026-01-21 (owner: Eng)"

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need legal language for Reserved capacity multi-year discounts (follow up with contracts).
- Confirm if Solutions will join all enterprise renewals or only high-risk accounts.
- Iterate on playbook phrasing to reduce talk-time and increase asks-per-meeting.

Next steps (short):
1) Create Google Slides templates for Standard + Enterprise (Daniel) — due EOD Wed
2) Build initial tracker sheet and import sample pilot accounts (Evan) — due Fri
3) Run 2 CSM pilots and collect feedback (Marisol) — week 2
4) Finalize playbook language and post to Confluence (Priya) — after pilot

If you are reviewing: please add comments inline in the slides link and ping me on Slack (@priya.nair) for synchronous review.

-- end of draft sprint kit --
